notes: Direct HTTP fetch throughout. Two Spanish sale-type sections exist, distinguished per the Sale-vs-Clearance test: (1) /rebajas/ (cgid=rebajas) - a huge, storewide biannual sale event: og/meta reads generically 'Rebajas', data-products-count=1029, and the category sitemap shows a rebajas-prefixed sub-tree mirroring virtually the ENTIRE site taxonomy (furniture indoor+outdoor, kitchen, bath, dining, lighting, storage, decor - 50+ rebajas/* URLs). No permanence language anywhere on the page (no 'liquidacion', 'fin de temporada', 'agotar existencias', 'ultimas unidades'). This is the classic Spanish twice-yearly 'temporada de rebajas' storewide markdown event, not a curated clearance/outlet concept - EXCLUDED as generic temporary promotional sale per brief Sec 3, not recorded as a row. (2) /special-price/ (cgid=ofertas-permanentes - note the site's OWN internal category id literally says 'permanentes' = permanent) - og:title 'Special Price Hasta -60% | Casa Viva', a much smaller, structurally distinct set (parent data-products-count=59 vs rebajas' 1029; only 1 of 32 sampled special-price product IDs also appears among 32 sampled rebajas IDs, confirming these are different populations, not the same sale under two URLs). The 'permanentes' taxonomy id is treated as the strongest available signal of standing/permanent-markdown intent on this site (no on-page copy states it explicitly) so this qualifies as Clearance. Also checked and excluded: /campanas/ofertas-flash-con-precios-black/ (Black Friday flash-price campaign page, found via sitemap - excluded as seasonal promo per brief), site search for 'outlet' (302-redirects to /novedades/?prefn1=conDescuento&prefv1=En%20Oferta, i.e. a discount FILTER on the New Arrivals listing, not a standalone clearance PLP - excluded as arbitrary filter page), site search for 'liquidacion' (no results). URL guesses /outlet/, /liquidacion/ both 404 directly. Sub-structure: special-price has 4 genuine site-defined department children (Cocina/Comedor/Muebles/Salon y Decoracion) confirmed via the refinement links on the parent page and cross-checked against sitemap. Parent page is a rollup: all 32 sampled parent-page product IDs are a subset of the 57 combined child-page IDs (0 parent-only IDs) - same recursive/aggregate parent pattern documented for this SFCC site in the prior Home-Decor pass notes (notes/120.md) - so the parent is emitted as a grouping row with qty=null, and only the 4 leaf pages carry qty.
